quote: for 50-minute CBRs, 50-minute counter-behavior, you're just doing the exact same thing on the hourly counter-behavior reversal, but you're just doing it in one fourth of time
interpretation: The 15m CBR is the hourly CBR applied to a 15-minute candle; durations scale by 1/4. The hourly course is a prerequisite and supplies definitions the 15m course assumes.

quote: the candle opens it extends uh for the first half around the second half you have that shift and then you're looking can do target back in towards 50% of this extension
interpretation: Core sequence: (1) 15m candle opens, (2) price extends in one direction during the first half, (3) a shift (reversal of low-timeframe structure) forms around the second half, (4) target a retrace toward 50% of the extension.

quote: on an hourly 10 plus hour range a middle time frame range on a 15 minute cbr we're looking for a around a 1.5 to 2.5 hour range maybe around 90 minutes or more of range ... four hour ... around 20 plus plus hours
interpretation: Condition range durations by model: 15m CBR ~ low-timeframe range 1.5-2.5h (~90+ min); hourly CBR ~ middle-timeframe range (5-)10+h; 4h CBR ~ high-timeframe range 20+h.

quote: high timeframe range is 20 hours, middle timeframe, five to 10 and low timeframe, 1.5 to 2.5
interpretation: Restates range tiers: HTF 20h, MTF 5-10h, LTF 1.5-2.5h.

quote: it's not just like the timeframe of the range that you're looking at. It's also the frequency of highs and lows within that time
interpretation: Range tier is identified by the number of swing highs/lows per unit time, not just duration. Higher frequency => lower timeframe range. Example counts: ~6 vs ~12 highs/lows in ~1-1.5h. Swing definition not given here.

quote: 36 swings tends to be pretty good um if you know gets higher than that tends be more of a low time frame sort of thing
interpretation: '36' is '3-6 swings' - confirmed by on-screen slide at 00:10:52 (see E15-048). Window length for the count: slide context implies the LTF range window (1.5-2.5h).

quote: you never want to catch the first candle behavior reversal within a range you want to catch like maybe the third or the fourth CBR within the range
interpretation: Do not take the first CBR in a range. Prefer the 3rd/4th; 2nd acceptable if more aggressive. Requires counting prior CBRs of the same model within the current range.

quote: look over the past you know 1.5 to 2 plus hours of price action and see if there's been previous 15 minute cbrs ... if you're looking to take a cbr and there's been no cbrs prior to that you're probably trading in the wrong condition
interpretation: Condition filter: at least one (ideally 2-3 clean) prior 15m CBRs in the last 1.5-2+ hours. Lookback for hourly model: 5-10+ hours. Also: if the recent setups were of a different model size (e.g. many 15m CBRs but looking for hourly), wrong condition.

quote: ideally you want you know two one two three clean setups prior if there's no setups is probably a bad condition
interpretation: Ideal: 2-3 clean prior setups. Zero prior setups = bad condition. 'Clean' is not defined.

quote: if you're not sure of the market condition, if it looks kind of hard and it's just confusing, then don't trade
interpretation: No-trade when the condition is unclear. Inherently discretionary; must be represented as a discretionary flag, not a rule.

quote: direction doesn't really matter when you're trading reversals ... if we're trading against direction we want to be trading external to structure if we're trading [with direction] We want to be trading internal to structure
interpretation: Direction is not a filter; it changes entry location. Counter-direction trades must be external to structure (after taking external highs/lows); pro-direction trades may be internal.

quote: we're going to be either looking for sales in the upper half or buys in the lower half of the range
interpretation: In a LTF range: sells only in upper half, buys only in lower half.

quote: in ranges you tend to have breaks of structure in both directions ... in trending ranges you tend to just break structure in one direction ... you might not be correcting to you know 75 percent um you might be correcting to 50 percent
interpretation: Range: BOS in both directions, corrections ~75%. Trending range: BOS in one direction, corrections ~50%.

quote: how on average how much have we been pulling back it's been greater than 75 pretty you know less than 50 percent uh this is how you identify the range the trend
interpretation: Condition classification by average pullback depth over the lookback: >75% => range; <50% => trend. 50-75% presumably trending range (inferred, not stated).

quote: if i'm trading within a range i want to look for you know cbrs that are around 75 200 of the conditions ... don't really looking for cbrs within the midpoint ... trending range ... sales after we take out highs or ... buys around 50 to 75 percent
interpretation: Range: CBRs at 75-100% of the range (near highs/lows; '75 200' read as '75 to 100'), avoid midpoint. Trending range (bullish example): sells only after taking out highs; buys at 50-75% pullback. Mirror for bearish.

quote: you just want to take out an internal high first for a bit of a correction back in towards 50 but this is lower quality of a trade ... external break structure trading external to the range ... tend to be higher quality
interpretation: Taking out an external high/low before the reversal = high-quality CBR. Taking out only an internal high/low = allowed but lower quality. Quality tier, not a hard filter.

quote: you don't want to target the internal high if you're trading counter to direction or reversal. You want to target the external high
interpretation: Counter-direction reversal: target external high/low, not internal. (Possible conflict with 50%-of-extension target in E15-002; may be different reference swings.)

quote: for you know a 50 minute cbr you won't be looking for buys below the open of the 50 minute candle and sells above the open of the 50 minute candle
interpretation: As spoken this is the opposite of the model (a buy follows a bearish extension below the open). Likely misspoken: buys must be below the 15m open, sells above. Must be checked against the chart.

quote: you can look for levels, AOIs. They're not as important as making sure you're trading within the right area within the condition
interpretation: AOIs/levels are secondary to location within the range.

quote: you can look to align um some candles closures with that you can look to align um alley levels you know on previous alley candle closures um you can even use you know 15 minute uh candle closures
interpretation: Optional confluence: levels from prior hourly or 15m candle closures.

quote: you're looking for i'd say an extension around four to five minutes ... four to five minutes of extension, I wouldn't go any really lower than that
interpretation: 15m extension duration: 4-5 minutes minimum. Hourly equivalent: ~18-20 minutes.

quote: you only have two minutes of extension it's too quick too high volume ... around six minutes of extension uh you create a bit of structure
interpretation: Counterexample: 2 min extension too short (no structure to break). ~6 min acceptable.

quote: the size of your win is dependent on the size of the extension ... you want a decent high volume extension that is decisive you don't want to have to guess is this an extension
interpretation: Extension must be large and decisive; no numeric size given. Small extension => poor reward to 50%.

quote: you want it to have relatively high volume and then start to decrease in volume around the halfway point of the 15 minute candle ... So you can break that structure to then have that shift
interpretation: Good extension profile: strong/fast early, slowing near the 7.5-min mark, forming small structure that can then be broken. Too-fast (no structure) and grinding (slow trend) extensions are both bad. 'Volume' likely means speed/range of movement; not defined numerically.

quote: you can look for a high volume counter sequence a seconds time frame trend as well
interpretation: Extension may be judged as a high-momentum trend on the seconds chart.

quote: you can trade this anytime within the day. Pretty much on gold ... it's condition specific more than it is time specific
interpretation: No session filter for 15m CBR on gold; condition dominates.

quote: i tend to find a higher win rate when i'm trading any second half of the 15 minute candle so the halfway point is 7.5 minutes
interpretation: Preferred: shift/entry in the second half of the 15m candle (after 7.5 min). Stated as a preference from experience.

quote: the five minute candle opens it immediately dumps pushes bearish here and takes out this low ... i'm not the biggest fan of this because this could just be the five minute candle uh creating the bonawick to then flip
interpretation: Caution: a shift created by a 5m candle opening and immediately breaking structure may just be that 5m candle's wick before it flips. Prefer 5m candle behavior aligned with the 15m CBR.

quote: you can look to align five minute um candle behavior with a 15 minute kind of behavior ... you can even look for you know a five minute candle closure in your favor
interpretation: Optional confluence: 5m candle behavior (5m extension over prior 5m high/low, 5m close in trade direction) inside the 15m CBR.

quote: for 50 minute candle behavior you can trade it anytime within the hour you can trade it within the first 15 the second third fourth 15 minutes it's really dependent on again the condition but also the previous alley candle closure market structure
interpretation: Any of the four 15m candles in the hour is eligible; choice depends on condition and prior hourly close/structure.

quote: you can align line 15 minute cbrs with hourly cbrs around 22 37 52 minutes into the hour if you're looking to take it around seven minutes into the hour it tends to be best if you have a previous hourly structure
interpretation: Shift-time anchors within the hour: :07, :22, :37, :52 (each ~7.5 min into a 15m candle). :22/:37/:52 can align with an hourly CBR; :07 is best with prior hourly structure (hourly close in favor).

quote: because this is a bullish candle close, this is a bearish candle close that actually creates a level ... look for the open of the hour to immediately push bullish into the level here that aligns with 50 of this shift and look for some 15 minute cbr ... within the first seven minutes
interpretation: Model A (hourly structure): after an hourly shift, a bullish hourly close followed by a bearish hourly close forms a level; the next hour opens, pushes into that level (aligned with 50% of the shift), and a 15m CBR forms within ~the first 7 minutes. Uses 'type 1/2/3' shift terms defined in the hourly course.

quote: you have a bullish candle close it creates a level for the next 15 minute candle to open ideally in the first half create that top wick to react into and then push bearish
interpretation: Model B (15m structure): prior 15m close creates a level; next 15m candle opens, wicks into it (ideally first half), then reverses.

quote: most of the time on 50 minute counter behavior reversals i'm looking to like trade external to structure like a 50 minute counter open uh over extend to take out a high and then look for a shift back in towards 50 percent
interpretation: Default 15m CBR: 15m candle opens, over-extends to take out a high/low (external), shift back toward 50%. Internal-to-structure trades only when a prior hourly close is in favor.

quote: you can also take continuations ... you draw out 50 and you look for the account to open ... extend uh into 50 of the previous bullish move look for a second shift for continuation ... you can target below the previous low you don't have to target 50 percent
interpretation: Model C (continuation): 15m candle opens and extends against the prior move into >=50% of it, reaction around the halfway point, seconds shift entry; target beyond the prior swing extreme (not 50%). Used in trendy conditions.

quote: i wouldn't take 15 minute candle behavior that is trading against hourly candle behavior ... i would look to avoid trading 50 minute cbrs against alley cbrs you kind of want to align them as much as possible
interpretation: No-trade: a 15m CBR against an active hourly CBR (e.g. hourly candle created its bottom wick and is flipping bullish; do not sell the 15m reversal). The more alignment the better.

quote: instead of looking for a one minute type three shift, we are looking for a five second or 15 second type three shift. I tend to focus on five second type three shifts
interpretation: Entry trigger: a type 3 shift on the 5-second (preferred) or 15-second chart. Hourly model uses 1-minute type 3 shift. 'Type 3 shift' defined in hourly course.

quote: the smaller the shift likely take a breakout of like the second's low if it's high volume ... a bit low volume and you have a bit bigger of a shift i'll tend to wait for you know a bit of a pullback and maybe a bit of a fractional shift into 50 of this
interpretation: Small shift + fast market: breakout entry at the seconds low/high break. Bigger shift + slow market: wait for pullback into ~50% of the shift (fractal shift).

quote: you put a stop below the low ... if it's more reversal, depends on the extension, but I just tend to target 50% of the extension
interpretation: Stop beyond the extension extreme (low for buys). Reversal target: 50% of the extension. Pro-condition trades may target further (continuation).

quote: you don't want to have a really tight stop loss you want to give your your stop loss a bit of breathing room ... because you can get slipped a lot ... we're trying to win rate max here not trying to have the biggest risk reward
interpretation: Stops on seconds shifts should have buffer beyond the structural level (size unspecified). Stated objective: win rate / consistency over R:R.

quote: you have a five minute candle open, which creates the break of structure here ... it's a little bit less likely for it to fully play out ... i'd look to be more aggressive uh with uh taking profit
interpretation: If the shift came from a new 5m candle's open, take profit more aggressively (less likely to reach 50%).

quote: ideally, you want DXY to be range bound and a similar sort of range to gold. And you just want it to be moving in the opposite direction ... i want uh gold to open and extend bullish i want dxy to open extend bearish
interpretation: DXY confluence: DXY in a similar range condition, and its 15m candle extends opposite to gold's extension over the same candle; both expected to retrace toward 50%. Stated as 'ideally'.

quote: you don't necessarily necessarily need a second shift on dxy it's great if you have it but uh i mainly focus on on shift on the main pair over dxy
interpretation: DXY entry-model shift is not required; the gold shift is primary. DXY should show inverted condition/structure/candle behavior.

quote: gold pushing bullish we take out this high um but we also have dxy pushing bullish as well and so what does it result in results in a loss and a fake out
interpretation: Counterexample: gold and DXY extending in the same direction preceded a failed setup. (Single example; illustrative, not proof.)

quote: dxy shift bearish it pushes bearish but then we have gold just move sideways ... That would actually be a signal for me to look to exit that trade
interpretation: Exit signal: in a gold long, DXY moves strongly in the favourable direction but gold ranges sideways => consider exiting.

quote: maybe you want to be external like i look at dxy to also be external to um the structure if it's you know counter to dxy direction
interpretation: Entry relativity applied to DXY: if counter to DXY direction, DXY should also be external to structure.

quote: with 15 minutes CBRs. There's going to be four eight Twelve good setups per day ... you're probably going to struggle to get as good of a risk reward on 50 minute cbrs
interpretation: Author's expectation: 4-12 good 15m setups/day vs 1-3 hourly; lower R:R than hourly. Useful as a sanity check on signal frequency, not a rule.

quote: 3. FREQUENCY OF HIGHS AND LOWS | TOO LOW 1-2 swings Range too big Sit out | SWEET SPOT 3-6 swings Target this condition | TOO HIGH 7+ swings Lower TF range Adapt entry
interpretation: Swing-count bands for the range window: 1-2 = range too big, no trade; 3-6 = target condition; 7+ = lower-timeframe range, adapt entry model. Swing detection method still undefined.

quote: Look back 1.5 to 2 hours and count how many clean 15-min CBRs set up and played out. 3+ clean setups in that window: good condition. Zero setups in the last hour: bad condition. Sit out. CBRs do not appear alone. They roll in packs.
interpretation: Condition score from prior setups: lookback 1.5-2h; >=3 clean 15m CBRs that 'set up and played out' = good; 0 in last hour = no trade. 'Played out' uses outcomes of PRIOR setups, which are known at decision time (no lookahead) but requires defining 'played out' (e.g. reached 50% target). 1-2 prior setups: not classified by slide; speech allows taking the 2nd if aggressive (E15-007).

quote: Never guess the start of a range. Wait for it to become obvious, then trade the later legs. Target legs 3, 4, and 5 into the range. Not legs 1 or 2.
interpretation: Only trade the 3rd-5th leg into a range. Slide says not leg 2; narration (E15-007) says '2nd if more aggressive'. Minor conflict -> open question. Leg counting requires a range-start definition.

quote: identify a middle time frame range ... Wait for a overextension into the high or low of that model of that range ... and then taking an entry around 30 to 45 minutes on into the hour that the overextension has occurred on
interpretation: Three-step hourly CBR: (1) identify an MTF range, (2) wait for an overextension into its high or low, (3) enter ~30-45 minutes into the hour in which the overextension occurred.

quote: 1. Identify MTF Ranging Condition [-> Range condition: 50% of prev move or more; MTF (5hrs-12hrs)] | 2 Wait for an hour candle open to overextend into high or low of the range [OE? -> around 2 15 min intervals push in one direction] | 3 Wait for T3 Shift, at AOI around half way point of the hour [T3 shift 20-45m -> 1m T3, 50% pullback, 5s T3 Fractal Shift or HVCS into HILO] | Correlation | SL beyond external H/L | TP target 50% of prev move
interpretation: Canonical master slide. Range = MTF 5-12h with corrections >=50%; OE = hour candle opens and pushes one direction for ~two 15-min intervals; entry = type-3 shift at an AOI 20-45 min into the hour via (a) 1m T3 + 50% pullback + 5s T3 or (b) HVCS into HILO; correlation check; SL beyond external H/L; TP 50% of previous move.

quote: HVCS->HILO 1. HVCS, 4+ mins 2. Goes beyond prev LTF/MTF HIGH 3. After 15m open, PA create wick/pushes a bit more 4. HILO beyond structure, entry on BOS of HILO 5. Target 50% of prev LTF move | Counter 1m trend or within larger shift
interpretation: Entry model A (HVCS->HILO): (1) high-volume candle sequence lasting >=4 minutes, (2) price goes beyond the previous LTF/MTF high (low for buys), (3) after a 15m candle opens, price creates a wick / pushes a bit further, (4) a HILO forms beyond structure; enter on the break of structure of the HILO, (5) target 50% of the previous LTF move. Used counter to the 1m trend or within a larger shift.

quote: two sub-edge models a high volume counter sequence into a high low technically that's a second shift in market structure or a one minute type three kind of like a fractal shift where you pull back towards 50% of that one type three with a high low or second shift within that
interpretation: Two entry models: (A) HVCS into HILO (a seconds-chart shift); (B) 1m type-3 fractal shift, pullback toward 50% of it, then a HILO or seconds shift inside that pullback. 'Counter sequence' = candle sequence (transcription).

quote: I define middle time frame as the past 5 to 12 plus hours ... Low time frame is defined by the past 30 minutes to an hour. High time frame is day plus
interpretation: Durations, not chart timeframes: LTF = 30-60 min of price action; MTF = 5-12+ h; HTF = ~1 day+. Author analyses on the 1m chart with a measure tool.

quote: anything under an hour i'd say there's lower time frame um anything over an hour to two is a lot more middle time frame you know even into to like four two three hours um high time frames like you know it would be this like whole move um half a day's worth or more
interpretation: Alternate move-size tiers used for entry relativity: LTF move <1h; MTF move 1-4h; HTF move half a day+. Conflicts with E1H-005 (MTF 5-12h) -> these tiers may refer to individual moves rather than conditions. Open question.

quote: if you're correcting around you know 50 or more of the previous move ... more of a trending range. If you're correcting like a lot more than 50%, like over 75 or even a hundred percent ... range bound side ... under 50% ... this would be more of a trend here ... 25% on average
interpretation: Condition by average correction of the previous move over the MTF window: >=75-100% = range; ~50-75% = trending range; <50% (~25%) = trend. Direction by highs/lows (HH/HL bullish, LH/LL bearish).

quote: A range is classified by ... correcting over 75% to maybe 100% ... then you have a trending range ... relatively clear direction ... but you're still correcting over 50% on average sometimes even 75% ... if you're unsure about direction ... it's probably just range bound
interpretation: Confirms E1H-007. Heuristic: if direction is unclear, the condition is probably a range.

quote: a middle time frame range reversal is defined by price action going sideways here going sideways for five to twelve plus hours so how do we identify ... we identify a range by it correcting over 50 of its previous move on average
interpretation: Looser statement: range = correcting >50% on average. Superseded in precision by E1H-007/008 (75%+ range, 50-75% trending range). Registered as a threshold discrepancy.

quote: fractal shift inverse versus fractal shifts as well this is just like a middle time frame shift that happens over the past five plus hours ... those are three types of middle time for models ... if i look at price action and it's none of these at all it just looks fucking weird ... i should not be trading if it's trending definitely shouldn't be trading
interpretation: Three MTF models: (1) range, (2) trending range (pro or counter), (3) fractal shift / inverse fractal shift. None identifiable, or a trend => no trade.

quote: inverse fracture shift and fractal shift um it's an inverse when you're you know you're trading the correction so if you're taking a buy here into 50 that's it inverse you're inversing that fractal shift
interpretation: Inverse fractal shift (IFS): after a large MTF impulse (type-3 shift), trade the correction back toward 50% of the impulse. Fractal shift (FS): wait for price to reach ~50% of the impulse and trade a lower-timeframe shift in the impulse direction (continuation).

quote: In a pro trending range, you're mainly looking for like an AOI, a shift for that pro trending range, continuation ... for counter trending range ... you want price to be below the lows ... there's not going to be an area of interest on average you just want it to be below or beyond structure
interpretation: Pro trending-range trade: at an AOI within structure (pullback). Counter trending-range trade: price must be beyond the external high/low; AOI not needed.

quote: each of these conditions can have different volumes ... I tend to like higher volume ranges more because there's a bigger move to catch ... i want to avoid like low volume ranges
interpretation: Prefer high-volume (large-swing) MTF ranges; avoid low-volume ranges. No numeric threshold.

quote: aoys this is just defined by the hourly candle opens and closes ... If there's lots of like, you know, AYs in the same sort of area, I'll just kind of draw a zone around it ... you get the the accuracy from your entry model
interpretation: AOI = hourly (also 30m, 4h) candle open/close prices; clusters become zones. Only AOIs at the range highs/lows matter in a range; in pro trending ranges an HTF candle-body level at the pullback. Precision comes from the entry model, not the AOI.

quote: entry relativity um is just how much we correct based on the previous move ... I'll say the upper half is 25% ... 25 50 of the previous move and then lower half is 75 of the previous move ... 25 is when you're buying and it's overextended don't want to do that middle time for like 50% of people's move good 75% really good
interpretation: Entry relativity = retracement depth of the previous move at entry, drawn from the move's origin to its extreme (extend the extreme until a >=50% correction occurs). Buckets 25% / 50% / 75%: 25% not advised (except trendy), 50% good, 75% very good (more range-bound). Journal field 'Entry Relativity: (LTF) 25% / (HTF) 50% (Middle) / (LTF) 75%'.

quote: i have a 40% win rate when i'm tracking taking a buy when it's only question should be 25% of the previous move here. If I'm doing 75%, a bit higher of a win rate
interpretation: Author's own journal statistic: ~40% win rate at 25% relativity, higher at 75%. Hypothesis to test, not a proven edge.

quote: external just means that you're um like beyond structure ... i find the best of reversals is when you take out the previous low um on the 50 minute candle
interpretation: External = beyond a prior high/low (LTF, MTF, or previous 15m candle high/low). Best reversals take out the previous 15m candle's high/low before shifting.

quote: We want it to overextend for around 20 minutes without much of a pullback at all ... i'll define a pullback is that you correct 50% of the previous move ... it's around 20 to 30 minutes of price action extending in one direction without a pullback
interpretation: Good hourly overextension: the hour candle opens (inside the range) and moves in one direction for ~20-30 minutes into the range high/low with no pullback, where pullback = a 50% correction of the move so far. Scales: daily ~10h, weekly ~2 days, 15m ~7.5 min (40-50% of candle length).

quote: if you see something like this where the alley counter opens and you go sideways for 30 minutes that's telling you that there isn't a trade ... pretty low volume and you're on average correcting 50% of the previous move ... this isn't a valid setup
interpretation: Invalid OE: hour goes sideways for 30 min, or low-volume push that keeps correcting ~50%.

quote: ideally you want the alley counter to open and not really push bullish ... you don't want much of a top wick at all because that will kind of delay the reversal and mess up timing
interpretation: Preference: minimal opposite wick at the start of the extending hour.

quote: My best setups is when the 30 minute candle or the third 15 minute candle opens and then immediately continues to push against me ... ideally i want to take out the previous low for a buy ... 37 minutes into the hour is the sweet spot for the best reversals
interpretation: Best setup: hour extends for the first half; the third 15m candle (opens :30) opens and continues against the trade, taking out the previous 15m low (buy) / high (sell); reversal around its halfway point (~:37).

quote: because we have the open of this 15 minute candle candle uh immediately pushing bearish to create that shift that's not what you want um you want the open of the 50 minute candle to continue pushing bullish take out the high and then to shift
interpretation: Counterexample: a shift created by the :30 15m candle opening straight in the trade direction (instead of first extending further) tends to fail around :37 as that 15m candle flips.

quote: the one example where you might not need um the the the previous counter the previous high um is if you have like a nice shift set up or nice 15 minute candle uh close bearish and then the next 15 minute candle kind of creating that top wick
interpretation: Exception: taking the previous 15m high/low is not needed if the previous 15m candle closed in the trade direction and the next 15m candle creates its opposite wick first.

quote: the general sort of rule that i'm looking for reversals is ... around 22 to 52 minutes ... The better reversals ... around 30 to 45 ... the best of the best reversals are around 37 minutes in
interpretation: Reversal (shift/entry) timing within the hour: acceptable :22-:52; better :30-:45; best ~:37. Quality increases toward :37. Slide: 'T3 shift 20-45m'.

quote: if the alley counter opens and it kind of you know fucks around for a and then pushes. Sometimes you can have the reversal happen a little bit later on ... If you have it open and immediately push, sometimes you have the reversal happen a bit earlier on, around 22 minutes in ... if it's high volume it could happen a bit earlier if it's low volume it could happen a bit later
interpretation: Timing shifts: immediate push / high volume / opening near the target range extreme -> earlier (~:22); delayed push / low volume / farther from the extreme -> later (:37-:52).

quote: ideally you want to be looking for continuations in the first 0-15 minutes, reversals 45 minutes ... Like if you don't have an overextension in a certain direction, there's no reaction or correction. You shouldn't be taking a reversal ... If you just go sideways on the on the hour candle if you create a wick in in both directions You shouldn't be taking that trade
interpretation: Continuations: first 0-15 min of the hour (after the opposite wick forms). Reversals: second half. No OE (sideways hour, wicks both sides) => no reversal trade regardless of the clock.

quote: looking for reversals um in the second half of the alley candle when the first half is massively pushed in one direction like you don't have to be right about direction ... If you're wrong about direction, the next alley candle is going to create the top wick first
interpretation: Rationale: a second-half reversal profits whether the hour candle flips (right on direction) or the next hour first creates its opposite wick (wrong on direction). Explains the 50% target.

quote: can pay the day i don't think this is actually that important ... don't worry about kind of behavior day um we're on low time frame moves so we'll track kind of behavior hourly
interpretation: Daily candle behavior is not important for the hourly model (conflicts in emphasis with daily/London CBOE material in E1H-038, which is a separate higher-timeframe setup).

quote: I always take an entry based off a shift in market structure ... If the shift happens over a couple minutes, like five minutes, I'll just say it's like a second shift because on the second time frame, you get more of a clear shift in direction
interpretation: Every entry requires a market-structure shift. A shift unfolding over ~5 minutes is read on the seconds chart ('seconds shift').

quote: a change in direction will be defined by a change in highs and lows so a shift if we're making bullish market structure high highs and higher lows if we take out a high into taking out low that would be a shift in direction
interpretation: Shift = in bullish structure, price takes out a high and then takes out a low (vice versa). This matches the 'type 3 shift' usage. Swing-point definition still unspecified.

quote: on a one minute shift i still want a clear um shift i want to take out high into taking out a low but my entry is going to be on the pullback towards 50 percent of this ... then i really want a reaction around that 50 area i want maybe second shift ... or i want a one minute high low ... you can put your stop loss behind the external high ... or ... above the the second shift
interpretation: Entry model B (1m fractal shift): 1m type-3 shift; wait for pullback to ~50% of the breaking impulse; require a reaction there (seconds shift or 1m HILO); stop beyond the external high/low (conservative) or beyond the seconds-shift swing (aggressive); target 50% of the previous move.

quote: if it's a higher volume condition you're more likely to go for a second shift ... one minute fractal shifts as an entry around 30 45 52 minutes in for second shifts they can happen around 22 to 37 minutes
interpretation: Model choice: high volume -> seconds shift (timing ~:22-:37); lower volume -> 1m fractal shift (timing ~:30-:52). Later: 1m shifts for pro-trend continuations, seconds shifts for counter-direction.

quote: If I have a 15 minute candle open and it mainly pushed for the first half bullish without creating a bottom wick at all, I will look to close around that halfway point of that 15 minute candle
